title: Your first graph
description: Build one node, connect it to the graph boundary, and inspect its state update.
tradeoff: Why is graph construction separate from graph execution?

title: A state contract
description: Inspect declared fields and observe which state values a node updates.
tradeoff: TypedDict documents a contract but does not validate every value at runtime. Where should validation occur?

title: Update only what changes
description: Apply a partial state update and verify that unrelated fields survive.
tradeoff: Why return only changed fields instead of rebuilding all state in every node?

title: A pipeline with clear stages
description: Normalize a document, tokenize it, then compute a word count through three graph nodes.
tradeoff: What can go wrong if a consumer runs before the node producing its input?

title: Route by policy
description: Choose a billing or technical path using a deterministic routing node.
tradeoff: How do explicit routes differ from an unrestricted model selecting side effects?

title: Merge updates deliberately
description: Append findings with a list reducer and compare the result with overwrite semantics.
tradeoff: When should repeated updates append, replace, deduplicate, or reject?

title: Messages with identity
description: Use add_messages to preserve role and message identity through a graph.
tradeoff: Why does message identity matter when editing conversation state?

title: A bounded tool node
description: Run an allowlisted word-count tool inside an explicit graph, without executing supplied source code.
concept: tool schemas and controlled graph execution
tradeoff: Does wrapping a function as a tool provide authorization or resource isolation by itself?

title: Repeat with a stopping rule
description: Execute a graph loop until the count reaches a validated target.
tradeoff: Why validate a business stopping condition as well as setting a recursion limit?

title: Read node updates
description: Inspect the updates stream as each graph node returns a state delta.
tradeoff: How do node updates differ from snapshots of the entire state?

title: Read evolving state
description: Inspect the values stream, including initial state and the snapshots after each update.
tradeoff: What does collecting a stream into a list lose compared with rendering events as they arrive?

title: Architecture you can inspect
description: Export graph structure as Mermaid and Graphviz while running the same compiled workflow.
tradeoff: Why is a graph diagram evidence of structure but not evidence of successful deployment?

title: The last state is available
description: Save a graph state in an in-memory checkpointer and read it by thread ID.
tradeoff: What failure destroys an in-memory checkpoint even when a thread ID is stable?

title: Two threads, separate histories
description: Write two states to one checkpointer and verify that thread IDs select the intended checkpoint.
tradeoff: Why is a thread ID an address for state rather than proof of authorization?

title: Checkpoints on disk
description: Write a graph checkpoint to SQLite and read it through a newly opened saver connection.
tradeoff: Which failures can one local SQLite file survive, and which need backups or replication?

title: Stop before the node
description: Persist a static breakpoint, inspect pending work, and continue on the same thread.
tradeoff: How does resuming a static breakpoint differ from supplying a dynamic interrupt decision?

title: Ask before proceeding
description: Pause with a review payload and resume with an explicit decision, retaining the original request.
tradeoff: Which parts of a node may execute again after resume, and where should side effects be placed?

title: Update and route together
description: Use Command to update the route field and choose the next graph node.
tradeoff: Why should destination names and return annotations agree?

title: A graph inside a graph
description: Compose a reusable normalization graph as a node in a parent workflow.
tradeoff: When should child and parent share a state schema, and when is an adapter preferable?

title: Configuration outside state
description: Inject a trusted multiplier through Runtime context rather than copying it into mutable graph state.
tradeoff: Why should authorization context come from a trusted caller rather than user-supplied state?

title: Two branches, one result
description: Run independent analysis branches with a reducer and join before composing the result.
tradeoff: Why is a reducer necessary for concurrent findings updates?

title: Map a changing workload
description: Fan out a dynamic list of values with Send, then reduce the results deterministically.
tradeoff: How would you preserve stable output ordering when task completion order is nondeterministic?

title: Replay from a known point
description: Find an intermediate checkpoint and replay the remaining graph steps from its saved configuration.
tradeoff: Which operations may run again during replay, and why do external effects need idempotency?

title: Edit a saved state
description: Update an intermediate checkpoint as a named node, then execute the remaining step.
tradeoff: Why does the node attribution influence which steps run after a state edit?

title: Compare two futures
description: Create two forks from one intermediate checkpoint and compare their outcomes without changing the original snapshot.
tradeoff: How would you distinguish exploratory forks from the production thread that may perform side effects?

title: Two decisions, one policy
description: Pause twice on separate review nodes and accept only when both decisions approve.
concept: separate interrupt stages and composite approval
tradeoff: When should rejection short-circuit later reviewers rather than collecting all decisions?

title: Memory beyond one thread
description: Store preferences under separate namespaces with the LangGraph store interface.
tradeoff: What trusted information should determine a namespace in a multi-tenant application?

title: Validate before orchestration
description: Enforce a Pydantic input boundary before creating and executing the graph.
concept: Pydantic validation at the graph boundary
tradeoff: Why is a TypedDict annotation insufficient for hostile external input?

title: Async work without shared mutation
description: Run asynchronous graph branches and merge their independent results.
tradeoff: Why does async execution not make CPU-bound work automatically faster?

title: Retry the right failure
description: Inject transient failures and let a bounded graph RetryPolicy recover.
tradeoff: Why can retries duplicate an external side effect even if the final graph state looks correct?

title: One operation, one receipt
description: Use a unique operation key and verify repeated graph execution does not duplicate a stored effect.
tradeoff: How should the system respond when one idempotency key is reused for different input?

title: An explicit fallback path
description: Route a failed primary operation to a declared fallback while preserving the failure reason.
tradeoff: When would returning stale fallback guidance be worse than failing the request?

title: A visible tool-call protocol
description: Create a model-style tool call, execute it with ToolNode, and route back to a response node.
tradeoff: Which part is deterministic protocol scaffolding here, and what would a live model add?

title: Validate before invoking tools
description: Reject unapproved names and malformed arguments before a real ToolNode sees a request.
tradeoff: Why should tool selection and tool authorization be separate checks?

title: Edit without duplicating turns
description: Use message IDs to replace one turn and remove another while retaining reducer semantics.
tradeoff: Why can blind list concatenation duplicate edited assistant turns?

title: A scoped specialist handoff
description: Use Command to hand a validated task to a named specialist and keep the handoff reason in state.
tradeoff: What context should be transferred to a specialist, and what should remain private?

title: Ground the response
description: Retrieve lexical evidence in one node, then compose a cited extractive response or abstain.
tradeoff: Why do source relevance, factual truth, and generated-answer correctness require different evaluation?

title: Execute an explicit plan
description: Validate a plan of allowlisted transformations, execute one step per graph loop, and record progress.
tradeoff: Why must a model-produced plan be validated independently before tool execution?

title: Keep a bounded context
description: Select recent messages within a character budget and keep a trusted policy outside history.
tradeoff: When does truncation require requesting shorter input rather than claiming the context was summarized?

title: Test behavior, not topology alone
description: Evaluate a routing graph against labeled cases and inspect per-example failures.
tradeoff: Which failures can remain invisible if you test only whether a graph compiles?

title: A job that resumes
description: Persist work between graph steps and advance a batch one unit at a time.
tradeoff: How do stable job IDs and replay-safe units make restart recovery possible?

title: Evolve persisted application state
description: Migrate an application payload inside a graph with explicit version checks and idempotent transformations.
tradeoff: Why must application-state migration be distinguished from serializer and dependency compatibility?

title: A durable memory namespace
description: Use a graph to save or read tenant-scoped preferences through transactional SQLite storage.
concept: durable namespaced memory and SQL parameters
tradeoff: Why is a correctly scoped storage key not a substitute for verifying the requesting tenant?

title: Reject a lost update
description: Update a record only when the caller holds the current version, using an immediate SQLite transaction.
tradeoff: When should a client retry automatically, and when must it reconcile the conflicting edit?

title: Record intent before dispatch
description: Commit a local outbox item and dispatch it exactly once to a local receipt ledger.
tradeoff: Why does local exactly-once recording not automatically guarantee exactly-once delivery to an external provider?

title: Approval needs permission
description: Require an eligible reviewer role before resuming a protected graph interrupt.
tradeoff: Why is an approve button insufficient without server-side identity and resource authorization?

title: A timeout is an outcome
description: Bound an async operation with wait_for and record a timeout without pretending it succeeded.
tradeoff: What happens if the underlying library ignores cancellation or performs a side effect before timeout?

title: Cache the right state
description: Cache a pure node by its complete input and verify identical inputs avoid repeated execution.
tradeoff: What authorization or freshness bug appears when a tenant or data version is omitted from a cache key?

title: Stop an overlong graph
description: Compare successful termination with GraphRecursionError when a graph exceeds its configured step budget.
tradeoff: Why does a graph step limit not replace a wall-clock timeout, token budget, or tool authorization?

title: An exportable graph
description: Invoke a graph exported for local HTTP serving and a future managed deployment workflow.
concept: graph exports and functional HTTP validation
tradeoff: Why does a manifest or a listening port not establish a working managed deployment?

title: Authenticate before authorizing
description: Verify a signed token and enforce tenant/role policy before executing a graph node.
tradeoff: How can a valid identity still lack permission for a resource?

title: Filter before exposing data
description: Select authorized tenant records before retrieval and ensure foreign records never reach a graph node.
tradeoff: Why is filtering model output too late if unauthorized data was already sent to the model?

title: Follow execution across spans
description: Attach a local RunTree hierarchy to a graph and optionally create/read back a redacted LangSmith run.
tradeoff: Why does a local trace ID not prove that a cloud run was received?

title: Stop before spending the budget
description: Account for declared per-step costs and terminate before a planned step would exceed the cap.
tradeoff: How would you reconcile estimated cost with actual billed token usage?

title: Preserve partial evidence on failure
description: Capture successful stream updates before a later node fails, without returning a fabricated final answer.
concept: partial stream evidence and explicit failure
tradeoff: How should a client distinguish partial updates from a completed response?

title: A functional workflow
description: Use LangGraph entrypoint and task decorators to express a checkpoint-capable functional workflow.
tradeoff: When is a functional API clearer than an explicitly declared StateGraph?

title: Reusable specialist graphs
description: Compose separate analysis and review subgraphs, then synthesize their state outputs in a parent graph.
tradeoff: What coupling appears when all specialist graphs share one large state schema?

title: Verify what you saved
description: Write an artifact through a graph node, record its SHA-256 digest, and verify the bytes after reopening.
tradeoff: Why does a matching digest establish byte integrity but not source authenticity or semantic truth?

title: Evaluate before release
description: Use a labeled dataset and an explicit quality threshold to gate a local candidate release.
tradeoff: Why must a release gate account for dataset coverage as well as an aggregate pass rate?

title: Measure every stage
description: Instrument a graph with stage events, errors, and wall-clock durations without logging input content.
tradeoff: Why should monitoring distinguish the primary failure, fallback behavior, and final user-visible outcome?

title: Support with a review boundary
description: Route support requests, pause financial work for approval, and keep a durable thread history.
tradeoff: What additional identity and payment-system controls are required before any real financial action?

title: Evidence before publishing
description: Retrieve a supplied document collection, draft a cited extract, and apply a coverage gate before recording publication eligibility.
tradeoff: Why does meeting a source-count threshold not prove that a claim is supported?

title: A research and critique team
description: Run separate evidence and critique branches, join their findings, and preserve uncertainty in the final brief.
tradeoff: Why should the synthesizer preserve the critic’s uncertainty rather than smoothing it away?

title: A recoverable batch pipeline
description: Validate a batch, transform each item through Send, and persist a content-addressed result for replay-safe reuse.
concept: dynamic batch work and idempotent results
tradeoff: How would you coordinate two workers racing to create the same job ID?

title: An observable release workflow
description: Combine graph execution, labeled evaluation, a release gate, and a durable decision ledger.
tradeoff: How would you expand this gate to cover quality, safety, latency, and deployment rollback separately?
